item.title: Travis Scott’s Cactus Jack Sets November 18 Heat Jersey Drop
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Travis Scott's Cactus Jack fan uniform drops at Miami's November 18 game, a day before the GTA album featuring his song "RHYNO."
item.content:encoded:
Travis Scott’s Cactus Jack is heading into the Miami Heat’s Vice City night with a Nike fan uniform set for a November 18 release at Kaseya Center. The drop gives his brand a retail date alongside his music in the Grand Theft Auto VI rollout.

The Swingman jersey carries pink “Vice City” lettering, a “VI” mark and six pink stars. The players’ version keeps the Heat name, with a reversed Nike Swoosh and Cactus Jack details. Matching shorts accompany both designs.

The fan uniform is part of a larger merchandise campaign. The surrounding Court Culture catalog lists products from several other collaborations, including a $55 Court Culture x Duvin “Vice City Pool Service” pocket tee and a $50 Court Culture x New Era “Vice City” snapback.

A Court Culture x The Wild Collective satin bomber is listed at $168. Those are separately branded pieces in the broader Vice City collection, while the Nike x Cactus Jack uniform is tied to the November 18 event. The different product names matter for fans following Scott’s contribution to the campaign.

His recording role is already in place.

“RHYNO,” produced by Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, was among the first six singles introduced for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album on September 17.

The album brings together 34 original tracks through a partnership with Atlantic Records, with a November 19 release alongside the game.

Its opening batch of singles also included Yung Lean’s “That’s It,” featuring Future and Metro Boomin, and music from PinkPantheress, Morgan Wallen, Rauw Alejandro and Keith Richards.

The Heat host Milwaukee on November 18, with tipoff set for 7 P.M. Eastern and a custom Vice City court planned for the night. The fan jersey will go on sale at the arena in limited quantities.

The music follows on a separate retail schedule the next day: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album is due on vinyl and CD as well as streaming services, with liquid-filled and splatter vinyl editions among the announced formats.

item.title: Gazir Sets Guinness Record With 197 Rap Battle Wins In 12 Hours
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Gazir won 197 of 200 freestyle battles in a Guinness record challenge with four extended breaks of four minutes each.
item.content:encoded:
Gazir earned a Guinness World Records title after 200 freestyle battles, completing a challenge with four four-minute rest breaks. He finished with 197 wins and three losses.

The November 7 event at Laboral Ciudad de la Cultura in Gijón, Spain, gave him the record for the most rap battles contested in 12 hours, according to EFE.

To complete the challenge, Gazir needed at least 190 wins, leaving room for 10 defeats. His final score put him seven victories above that target, with a 98.5 percent win rate across the day.

The format also explains why 200 battles meant facing 250 opponents. He had 150 one-on-one contests and another 50 against two MCs at once. Those matchups were split into 10 blocks, each containing 20 battles.

Gazir had described the appeal in a pre-event EFE interview.

“There are skills in my freestyle I don’t have time to show in four battles,” he said, translated from Spanish.

A speech therapist, singing teacher, physical trainer, nutritionist and psychologist helped him prepare for the attempt.

The basic format had MCs trading four-bar turns, with six turns per side.

Judges had to pick a winner without an extra tiebreak round, and the schedule left 20 seconds to move from one battle to the next.

The longer breaks came after every 40 battles: four four-minute pauses. Hosts, DJs and judges rotated during those stops, while Gazir remained the only competitor required to complete the full run.

Babi, Skone and Bnet accounted for his three defeats.

“My job is to ensure each battle is legal,” the Guinness adjudicator told EFE during the event, translated from Spanish.

The audience helped choose the last obstacle.

Voting opened October 21 to select Gazir’s final opponent, and fans picked Mexican MC Aczino, whose three international Red Bull Batalla championships came in 2017, 2021 and 2022.

That last title had come at Gazir’s expense in the 2022 international final in Mexico City. Four years later, Aczino faced him in battle 200, in a lineup that placed a national champion or international podium finisher at the end of each block.

item.title: Bradford Cohen Calls For Lil Durk’s Release After AllHipHop Contraband Report
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Bradford Cohen urged Lil Durk's release and criticized prosecutors' contraband argument after sharing AllHipHop's reporting.
item.content:encoded:
Bradford Cohen called for Lil Durk to be released on bond after sharing AllHipHop’s report on the federal contraband investigation prosecutors cited in their fight to keep the rapper jailed.

The criminal-defense attorney used his @lawronin Instagram account to criticize the government’s reliance on alleged jail-rule violations, arguing that the claims were a familiar way to oppose release when the underlying case was weak.

“This is one of the oldest plays in the game. When your argument is weak say the Defendant cant even follow instructions in the prison,” Cohen wrote.

His post displayed AllHipHop’s November 4 story, “Lil Durk Faces Contraband Investigation As Feds Fight His Release.”

That report detailed prosecutors’ allegations that Durk used unauthorized communication devices and helped bring contraband into the Metropolitan Detention Center in Los Angeles.

Prosecutors argued that his conduct in custody showed he would not follow restrictions outside jail. They accused him of making hundreds of unauthorized calls, using other inmates’ phone access and refusing a cell search.

Cohen rejected the government’s framing.

“Makes the government look petty in this case as they were already losers,” he wrote.

The reference followed Durk’s September 11 acquittal on all five charges tried in the murder-for-hire prosecution arising from the 2022 Los Angeles shooting that killed Saviay’a “Lul Pab” Robinson. Prosecutors had accused Durk of financing an attack targeting Robinson’s cousin, Quando Rondo.

Lil Durk remained detained on separate murder-in-aid-of-racketeering and firearm charges, including allegations tied to Stephon Mack’s January 2022 killing in Chicago. He pleaded not guilty, and the remaining trial was set for August 30, 2027.

Cohen’s criticism went beyond the contraband claims. He argued that prosecutors applied their public-safety concerns differently when defendants agreed to cooperate and described pretrial detention as pressure to strike a deal.

“Bond is for the most part used as leverage. Leverage to flip and leverage to plea,” Cohen wrote.

Durk’s lawyers offered future music royalties, publishing income and earnings from his name, image and likeness as security for his release. The proposal also included property and assets pledged by supporters, with Sony backing a guarantee capped at $1 million.

Jay-Z submitted a letter supporting release, while J. Cole and former Cook County State’s Attorney Kim Foxx also backed the request. Robinson’s family said it did not object if the court considered bond appropriate.

Judge Michael W. Fitzgerald heard arguments on November 4 and took the request under submission without immediately ruling. The prosecution opposed release based on its assessment of flight risk, public safety and the alleged conduct in custody.

Cohen backed the defense proposal and urged the judge to approve it.

“The judge should GRANT him a bond. This is a very strong bond package. If he does, this will be another ding in the governments case. They need to just cut bait,” he wrote.

item.title: Adrien Broner Reportedly Okay, DeenTheGreat Weighs Going Solo
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Adrien Broner's stream partner DeenTheGreat weighed a solo path as he questioned claims about a bag after the concert scare.
item.content:encoded:
Adrien Broner is doing okay and managed to avoid a hospital stay after a crazy video showed him passed out in a wheelchair.

The former four-division boxing champ needed help during a night out on Saturday, November 7.

He was at Skilla Baby’s “The Price of Fame Tour” stop at The Belasco in Los Angeles.

As the night played out on a Kick stream, medics tended to Broner and others helped him down a flight of stairs.

He was placed in a wheelchair and taken out of the venue.

In related news, Blueface denied rumors his crew stole Broner’s bag, supposedly holding $50,000 to $100,000, on his Sunday stream, TMZ reported.

DeenTheGreat, Broner’s stream partner, asked if there was any cash in the bag.

He spoke in a video posted on his own channel Sunday, as he went through clips and claims about the night.

“I don’t know if he had bread in that, though,” Deen said.

He warned that short clips could leave out key parts of a night. He also said the bag could have been returned and then lost.

Deen spoke about the strain on their work together. He said Broner had to want to change and suggested working with other people if that did not happen.

While he pushed back at taking blame for Broner’s choices, he credited their on-screen chemistry with drawing in fans.

Their work had already moved beyond streams.

On October 15, Broner joined Deen and producer Hitmaka on “Purple App Killa,” a song aimed at Kai Cenat. The official upload listed both men as collaborators. They appeared in its video after sharing clips of work on the song.

In that Sunday upload, Deen said Broner was missing a key week for them, with New York radio shows ahead.

He linked that concern to what he saw as a lack of commitment from Broner. He said fans had seen how much he had tried to help.

That was why he raised the chance of going solo. Deen said it was hard to keep working with Broner, but left room for the two to link up from time to time.

“I love you as a brother, business partner, whatever, bro,” he said.

item.title: MC Lyte’s VH1 Jacket Enters Rock Hall Exhibit
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: MC Lyte's 2006 VH1 Hip Hop Honors jacket joins the Rock Hall exhibit, with free local access offered on November 22.
item.content:encoded:
MC Lyte‘s jacket from the 2006 VH1 Hip Hop Honors is among the pieces in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame’s new inductee exhibit, bringing a career tribute into the museum.

Axios Cleveland identified the jacket as one of the artifacts. The museum set November 9 as the exhibition’s official opening, after a members-only preview on November 6. The show represents all 18 members of its 2026 induction class.

The jacket reaches back to a night when younger women in rap performed Lyte’s music in her honor.

At the 2006 ceremony at New York’s Hammerstein Ballroom, Lil’ Kim, Remy Ma and Da Brat covered “Lyte as a Rock.” Lyte was an honoree alongside artists including Rakim, Beastie Boys and Wu-Tang Clan.

AllHipHop covered that tribute at the time. It put Lyte’s records in the hands of another generation of rappers, with her own performance part of the show; 20 years later, an item from that evening is part of another institution’s account of her career.

Her recording milestones include the 1988 debut Lyte as a Rock, followed by Eyes on This in 1989 and the Grammy-nominated “Ruffneck.”

Those records established a catalog she has continued to bring to live audiences while working as an actress, DJ and entrepreneur.

The current celebration also runs through her Road To The Hall Of Fame tour. Its Atlanta bookings at City Winery fall on November 9 and 10, with both shows listed for 8 P.M. Eastern time. The venue lists both nights as sold out and offers a waitlist.

In AllHipHop’s September tour interview, Lyte outlined roughly 90-minute shows with stories and conversation alongside her catalog.

She planned to carry those sets without depending on guest appearances. Her September studio update also put her back to work with producer Warryn Campbell.

The Rock Hall ceremony is set for November 14 at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater.

In Cleveland, Cuyahoga County residents can visit the museum free with an RSVP on November 22, from 10 A.M. to 5 P.M. That community day includes the new exhibit, select “Soul Train” footage and performances by artist-in-residence alumni.

item.title: Nelly Explains How Booze Helped Him Beat Allen Iverson In Game Of Horse
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nelly revisits his HORSE win over Allen Iverson, admitting alcohol and Jermaine Dupri's low ceiling helped shape the upset.
item.content:encoded:
Nelly is taking some of the shine off his famous HORSE win over Allen Iverson. The St. Louis rapper admitted alcohol, a familiar gym and a low ceiling all helped him beat one of basketball’s great scorers.

Nelly revisited the game during an episode of “7PM in Brooklyn with Carmelo Anthony.” The matchup happened at Jermaine Dupri’s home gym in Atlanta during the offseason, after both men had spent the night out.

“We was playing HORSE, but in fairness, did I beat him? Yes, I beat him playing HORSE. But we was both hammered, he was just hammered,” Nelly said in the show’s official clip.

The admission did not erase his victory. It explained how a rapper who openly admitted he couldn’t defend Iverson still managed to win a shooting contest against him.

Nelly knew Dupri’s court and understood its limits. Iverson kept using the high arc that worked in NBA arenas, but the roof repeatedly got in the way. Nelly adjusted to the room and leaned on the set shot he had practiced there.

The format also narrowed the gap between them.

HORSE rewards shot-making instead of defense, with one player choosing a shot and the other trying to match it. That let Nelly use his local knowledge without having to stay in front of one of the NBA’s quickest guards.

That familiarity became his real advantage. Nelly described himself as a reliable shooter who could stand in one spot and keep making shots, even if guarding Iverson was out of the question.

He also acknowledged that beating a fully prepared Iverson would have been a different task.

Iverson eventually removed the excuses. Nelly said the Hall of Famer returned sober for a rematch and beat him decisively, ending any idea that the first result settled who was better on the court.

item.title: Yella Beezy Begins Defense After Judge Refuses To Dismiss MO3 Case
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Yella Beezy's defense called its first witness after prosecutors rested and a judge denied a bid to dismiss the MO3 case.
item.content:encoded:
Yella Beezy‘s defense began presenting its case Monday, November 9, after Judge Chika Anyiam rejected a request to dismiss the MO3 capital murder case in Dallas for lack of evidence.

Prosecutors had rested after Detective Eric Barnes finished testifying. The defense then called Hitco Entertainment employee Lynn Scott as the defense’s first witness, according to FOX 4.

Yella Beezy, whose legal name is Markies Conway, pleaded not guilty to capital murder and denied involvement in MO3’s death. Prosecutors accused him of paying Kewon White to carry out the killing.

MO3, born Melvin Noble, was killed on Interstate 35E in Dallas on November 11, 2020. White was convicted on September 4, 2026 and sentenced to life without parole.

Earlier, Judge Anyiam excluded a jailhouse call by Kewon White that prosecutors sought to introduce.

Attorney Toby Shook also challenged Barnes over calls with witness Jose Bodega in 2025 and 2026, including one lasting 82 minutes and another lasting 70 minutes at 4:48 A.M. Barnes acknowledged keeping no written notes.

The defense suggested Bodega had received improper guidance and support. The detective denied a personal friendship with Bodega and said the witness felt isolated and threatened after being identified online. Barnes said he had never spent so much time talking with a witness.

Bodega, born Theodore Thomas, is Yella Beezy’s childhood friend and a witness who has already disavowed his own grand jury account of the alleged plot to kill MO3.

On November 2, Bodega testified under immunity and recanted the claims he had made to a grand jury on February 13, 2025.

He told jurors he fabricated his earlier account that Yella Beezy and Trapboy Freddy wanted MO3 dead.

Bodega had invoked his Fifth Amendment rights outside the jury’s presence on October 29. He had agreed to cooperate through a separate federal drug case, a connection the defense explored before the murder trial began.

Judge Anyiam had allowed prosecutors to question Bodega as a hostile witness.

The jury’s use of his earlier statements was limited: jurors could consider them when judging his credibility, not as proof that the events he had described actually happened.

item.title: Kodak Black Confirmed For GTA VI As Role Stays Under Wraps
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kodak Black and Bradford Cohen confirmed his GTA VI appearance, adding a clear new fact to Rockstar's unnamed launch image.
item.content:encoded:
Kodak Black has confirmed that he appears in Grand Theft Auto VI, adding the artist’s own word to a launch image that Rockstar Games published without a caption.

Kodak and his attorney, Bradford Cohen, confirmed the appearance in a social media video.

That confirmation adds the key detail confirming AllHipHop’s November 6 coverage of Rockstar’s launch gallery. At the time, the official image showed a man whose face tattoos, hair and 1800 Block chain closely resembled the Pompano Beach rapper.

Rockstar did not name the figure, and Kodak had not publicly described his involvement.

Rockstar released the gallery on November 5 as part of the final two-week push toward the game’s November 19 launch. Its announcement directed fans to a larger collection of screenshots from Vice City and the wider state of Leonida, but it did not identify the people shown in those images.

Kodak’s confirmation strengthens the identification but doesn’t fill in the rest of the picture.

Rockstar has not announced a character name, credited him as a voice actor or described a mission tied to his appearance.

The South Florida connection gives the cameo a natural setting. Kodak, whose legal name is Bill Kapri, is from Pompano Beach.

GTA VI returns the series to Vice City, Rockstar’s fictional version of Miami, and expands the map across a Florida-inspired state.

The studio has used regional music, landmarks and nightlife throughout the rollout. Kodak’s music was already connected to the game before the gallery appeared, but the new confirmation places the rapper himself inside the world Rockstar has built.

Players will get their first chance to see how much of Kodak’s appearance survived into the finished game when Grand Theft Auto VI arrives November 19.

item.title: Donald Trump Says He Would Rather Go To Hell Than Forgive His Enemies
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Donald Trump told 60 Minutes he may never forgive some political enemies, even under a hypothetical tied to heaven.
item.content:encoded:
Donald Trump said he may never forgive some political enemies, even when asked to imagine that forgiveness as the final condition for entering heaven.

The exchange came during Trump’s first post-midterm interview with 60 Minutes correspondent Ross Douthat. The president said he considered himself religious, hoped to reach heaven and did not want to go to hell.

Douthat then offered a pointed hypothetical. He asked whether Trump could forgive figures such as former FBI Director James Comey and former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi if paradise depended on it.

Trump described those opponents as dishonest and harmful to the country. He cited his indictments, two impeachments and what he called the weaponization of government before answering.

“I probably cannot do that, no, because I do hate some of my enemies and I always will,” Trump said.

The question built on Trump’s remarks at Charlie Kirk’s September 2025 memorial service in Arizona. Kirk’s widow, Erika Kirk, had spoken about forgiving the man accused of killing her husband. Trump later told the crowd that Charlie Kirk wanted the best for his opponents, while he did not share that view.

That earlier line drew laughter at the memorial and was widely treated as a blunt description of Trump’s political style. More than a year later, Douthat returned to it as a question about faith, judgment and whether the president could separate personal grievance from Christian forgiveness.

Trump did not soften the answer. He said giving an easy yes would feel false, then argued that love of country outweighed any obligation he felt toward people he viewed as destructive.

Douthat pressed him by pointing to the success and advantages Trump had received during his life. The president still declined to promise forgiveness.

The full interview covered Republican midterm losses, immigration, the economy, Iran, Ukraine and possible successors to the MAGA movement. The forgiveness exchange stood apart because it placed Trump’s familiar complaints about political foes inside a religious test he accepted on his own terms.

Trump treated the hypothetical as a question about his own willingness to forgive before final judgment. His response left little ambiguity about the grudge itself.

item.title: EU Presses TikTok To Redesign Its “For You” Feed
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: TikTok's For You feed faces an EU redesign demand after regulators flagged harmful recommendation loops and weak user controls.
item.content:encoded:
TikTok is facing a European demand to rebuild parts of its For You feed after regulators said its recommendation system can pull users into repeated loops of harmful content.

The European Commission issued preliminary findings under the Digital Services Act, focusing on what it calls the feed’s “rabbit hole effect.”

The regulator said watching or liking certain videos can prompt TikTok to serve more of the same, including material about sadness, isolation, weight loss and body image.

Commission officials said TikTok did not adequately assess those risks or put effective safeguards in place, particularly for minors and vulnerable adults.

The proposed fixes reach into the feed’s basic machinery: give more weight to a user’s stated preferences, stop using viewing time as a recommendation signal, make controls easier to use and regularly test the algorithm.

The findings are preliminary.

TikTok can review the Commission’s evidence and respond before regulators make a final decision. A confirmed violation could expose parent company ByteDance to a fine of up to 6 percent of its global annual revenue.

TikTok rejected the Commission’s account in a statement to Reuters.

“The Commission has made a series of statements that are fundamentally inaccurate and distort our platform’s architecture and our commitment to user safety,” the company said.

For artists and listeners, the practical stakes sit in the distribution system. TikTok’s feed decides which clips surface repeatedly and which ones fall away, so changing the signals behind those recommendations could alter how music, dances and cultural conversations travel through the platform.

The Commission’s requested changes focus on recommendation inputs and user controls rather than individual songs or creators.

The case is part of a longer review of TikTok’s design.

In February, the Commission separately issued preliminary findings on features including infinite scroll, autoplay and push notifications. In July, it said the platform’s protections for minors also fell short of the Digital Services Act.

This latest stage narrows the dispute to the way the For You feed learns from engagement and repeats similar subjects. TikTok now has to answer the regulator’s evidence while the Commission decides whether those design changes become an enforceable order.
